summary: Counted N_p(T)=#{(a,c,d)∈Z³: ad−pc=1, 1≤c≤T, |a|,|d|≤T} exactly (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z2996.c, data z2996_out.txt) for p∈{13,409,577,1009,5569}, T=10³…2.56·10⁵. The coset-volume count in the DRS/EMM sense is therefore the T log T main term; its comparison with R(p) is not a like-for-like quantity (R(p) counts one prime's (★)-triples, N_p(T) counts a quadric in three variables), so no identification with R(p) follows.

summary: Counted the rational-form case directly: for the isotropic ternary form Q=ad−pc with value 1, N_p(T)/T increases by a constant amount per factor 4 in T (slope per unit of ln T ≈ 2.00 for p=409, 577, 1009, 5569; ≈1.85 for p=13), i.e. N_p(T) ~ c_p·T log T rather than the T^{n−2}=T rate of the generic (non-degenerate) EMM/DRS ternary count. summary: Read the abstract of Tseng (Math. Z. 302 (2022), arXiv:2106.00836, verified via arXiv API): a closed horocycle of length ℓ equidistributes on the cusp neighbourhood shrinking at rate T^{−1} whenever T/ℓ→0 (segment condition max{T^{−1/6},(T/ℓ)^{1/2}}(T/ℓ)^{−δ}, which is trivial for the full closed horocycle). So the deepest reachable target for a closed horocycle of length p has measure ≈1/T with T=p^{1−o(1)}, i.e. measure p^{−1+o(1)}, and the expected number of visits is ℓ/T=p^{o(1)}. Kelmer (arXiv:1708.08953) treats logarithm laws/shrinking targets for discrete flows and does not give the closed-horocycle depth.
not_done: Matching the ES target's normalisation (horocycle length and cusp height convention) to Tseng's T; the statement is about one horocycle of length ℓ, the ES family is p orbits.
next: Check bsA's target normalisation against Tseng's T and length ℓ; if they match, the ES-target depth p^{−1+ε} is inside Tseng's range.

summary: Read EXCEPTIONAL_SHORT Thm 2: E(I;q,b) ≤ C·q₁·(H/q)·exp(−c(log(H/q))^{3/4}), q₁ the X_q-smooth part of q. Requiring the exceptional count to be below the number of progression members H/(q log x) gives H(x) = q·exp(C′(log log x)^{4/3}) (superpolylogarithmic in x, ineffective constants). But this bounds primes in progressions failing equidistribution, not (★)-failures; applying it to (★) needs the (★)-failures to lie in that exceptional set, which the theorem does not give. So the smallest H obtained is for primes in progressions, and no (★)-prime bound follows.

summary: Wrote the (★) count as a sum over levels: R(p)=Σ_C #{d | 4Cp+1: d≡−1 (mod 4C)}, a divisor function in the progression −1 mod 4C with modulus q=4C and length N=4Cp+1. summary: Fibre argument: over a fixed level C the surface 4uBC−u−B=p is the hyperbola (4Cu−1)(4CB−1)=4Cp+1, a split torus G_m over Q, so the generic fibre has trivial Brauer obstruction and is locally soluble at every place with a divisor of 4Cp+1 in the right class; the integral obstruction therefore lives in the global divisor condition d≡−1 (mod 4C), not in Br. Checked against Z2943/Z2952 data: failing levels are not explained by local data. This is an argument, not a Brauer group computation of the total space.

summary: The reparametrisation is an identity: for a certificate (u,B,C) with d=4uC−1 and cofactor e=4BC−1 (de=4Cp+1), c_d/d := (4Cp+1)/(4Cp·d) = e/(4Cp) = k/(4p) with k = e/C = 4B − 1/C. So the variable k is the cofactor B up to a 1/C shift; parametrising the hits by k is the same as parametrising by B. Checked on 78 certificates for p∈{409,1009,10009,100049} (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_E.py, E_out.txt): d·e=4Cp+1 and k=4B−1/C hold with zero failures.
not_done: Clustering statistics (none needed once the parametrisations agree).
next: None.

summary: Single-character reduction of M_BM: regressing M_BM/M0 on the single Legendre symbol (ℓ/p) for primes 1e3<p≤10⁵ gives R²≤0.05 for every ℓ<60 (best ℓ=3: 0.050; ℓ=5: 0.012). The spread of M_BM/M0 is mean 0.97, min 0.557 (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_C.py, C_out.txt). A single real character therefore changes the main term by at most about 45% at this range, and a Landau–Siegel-type bound on one exceptional character would give at most a bounded factor.
not_done: Real-character decomposition beyond the Legendre symbols of primes below 60; the Siegel-zero analysis.
next: Regress on all real characters mod 4·ℓ for ℓ≤100.

summary: Image of positive solutions of 4xyz=n(xy+yz+zx) in U_n(Z/q) for n with ≥8 solutions (19 values of n, q∈{3,5,7,11}; scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z3163.py, Z3163_out.txt): the mean ratio |image|/|U_n(Z/q)| is 0.71 (q=3), 0.47 (q=5), 0.32 (q=7), 0.16 (q=11). The sample (8–30 solutions per n) is far smaller than |U_n(Z/q)|≈q², so the ratio measures sample size, not strong approximation; no conclusion about Brauer–Manin or strong approximation follows.
not_done: Solutions of U_n with large height (needs the full integral point set).
next: Enumerate integral points of U_n with height ≤10⁴ (not only positive ones) and redo the image count.

summary: Substitution a=ck−1, d=cl−1 in ad−pc=1 gives c(ckl−k−l−p)=0, i.e. ckl−k−l=p: the SL₂-quadric is birational to the (★)-cubic (u,B,C)↦(k,l,c) with 4C=c-type scaling. For fixed c the surface is the hyperbola (ck−1)(cl−1)=cp+1, a split torus, so it is not homogeneous under a group acting transitively on it; the substitution therefore identifies the object but does not produce a homogeneous variety.
not_done: Strong-approximation for the total space (not computed).
next: None unless a homogeneous model is proposed.

summary: Premise check on the count: the number of supersingular j-invariants in characteristic p is ⌊p/12⌋ plus 0, 1, 1 or 2 according to p mod 12 (≡1,5,7,11), the standard count matching the Eichler class number ≈p/12. The ES primes are p≡1 (mod 4) and the standard maximal-order normal forms (Pizer) are given for ramified primes p≡3 (mod 4); so the quaternion algebra attached to a given ES prime is not fixed by the repo, and the 'small-vector' test (norms of maximal-order vectors vs certificate divisors) has no defined map yet.
not_done: Explicit maximal orders and short-vector enumeration.
next: Choose the ramified prime q≡3 (mod 4) attached to each ES prime (or define the map) and enumerate norms ≤4p.

summary: F_p[T] search (p=3, deg P≤4; p=5, deg P≤3; scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z3175.py): for every monic irreducible P in these ranges there is a representation 4/P=1/X+1/Y+1/Z with X monic of degree ≤2n and Y,Z nonzero polynomials (reduced to a 2-term check via divisors of B²). No counterexample was found. Range is small; q=2 (characteristic 2 excluded by the repo's Lemma 1.1) and q=4 (not prime) were not searched.

summary: Exact orthogonality identity: for gcd(N,m)=1, Σ_{χ mod m} χ̄(−1)χ(d) = φ(m)·[d≡−1 (mod m)], so Σ_{χ≠1} χ̄(−1)σ_χ(N) = φ(m)·D⁻_m(N) − τ(N). Hence at any level with no certificate (D⁻=0) the nontrivial twisted sum equals −τ(N) exactly (ratio 1), and in general |Σ_{χ≠1}|/τ(N)=|φ(m)D⁻/τ(N) − 1|. The item's 'how close it gets' is therefore determined by D⁻: it is never small when D⁻=0. (Derived by orthogonality; not brute-force verified over characters.)
not_done: Brute-force character sum verification for hard p.
next: Verify the identity numerically with explicit characters for m≤40.

summary: Tested natural switch maps from (★)-triples (u,B,C) to unordered b=1 pairs {s,t} (B1 Lemma 1.1: st|p+s+t, 4|st): candidates {B,4uC}, {u,4BC}, {4uB,C}, {u+B,4C} on p∈{409,577,193,2521,1009,10009,5569} (scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z3182.py, Z3182_out.txt). The first three map to zero b=1 pairs; {u+B,4C} hits 8 of 17 at p=10009 and 0 elsewhere. No bijection between the two data sets was found.

summary: Root-of-unity expansion: 1[m|x]=(1/m)Σ_k e(kx/m) gives R(p)=Σ_{(u,C)}(1/m)Σ_k e(k(p+u)/m) with m=4uC−1; the k=0 term is S₀(p)=Σ_{m≤p+u}1/m over pairs (computed for all primes ≤10⁵: scripts/z52d_p2_TO8_Z3185.c, Z3185_out.txt). Window means: R = 12.8, 17.0, 21.0 with S₀ = 8.7, 11.8, 14.8, so the k≠0 remainder has mean R−S₀ = 4.1, 5.2, 6.2 (variance 24→58, correlation with S₀ only 0.14–0.27). The k=0 term carries about 2/3 of the mean; the remainder grows like ≈0.5·log p, which is an arithmetic (prime-in-progression) bias of the k≠0 terms, not decay.
not_done: A closed form for A_q(p) with Ramanujan sums; the bias source is not identified.
next: Compute A_q(p)=Σ_{k: gcd(k,q)=q?}-type terms for q≤100 and locate the growing bias.
